# Tool Registry

Tracks researched tools. Check before first use, update after research.

| Tool | Version | Date | Key Learnings |
|------|---------|------|---------------|
| Appium `wdaConnectionTimeout` | appium-webdriveragent 16.13.6 | 2026-10-06 | The capability is the `WebDriverProxy` per-request timeout applied to every proxied WDA command, including `POST /session` during session creation — not just the initial connection. A cold app launch can exceed 90 s and fail with "Unable to start WebDriverAgent session ... timeout of 90000ms exceeded". Keep the xcuitest driver default of 240 s (inside the client's five-minute session budget). `wdaStartupRetries: 1` deliberately disables xcuitest's startup retry loop, so this timeout is the only startup margin. |
| git-filter-repo | 2.47.0 | 2026-10-06 | `pip install --user git-filter-repo`; on Windows invoke the exe under `%APPDATA%\Python\Python312\Scripts` directly since it is not on PATH. Run on a fresh `git clone --mirror`; `--invert-paths --paths-from-file` strips paths across all refs including tags. Old objects stay in the pack until `reflog expire --expire=now --all` + `gc --prune=now`, so measure `size-pack` only after GC. Stripping this repo's generated dumps took the pack from 395 MB to ~15 MB. |
| git lfs migrate | git-lfs 3.7.1 | 2026-10-06 | `git lfs migrate import --everything --include=<globs>` rewrites every ref, converts matched blobs to LFS pointers, and appends LFS rules to `.gitattributes` in the rewritten commits. GitHub bills LFS to the repo owner: storage counts every migrated historical version (1 GB free), and each clone checkout downloads that revision's objects (1 GB/mo free); `actions/checkout` defaults to `lfs: false` and fetches pointers only. Migrating this repo's dumps produced a 9 MB pack with a 1.9 GB LFS store. |
| Cold Appium reader snapshot | XCUITest 12.15.0 | 2026-10-05 | In [merge-queue run 37353901272](https://github.com/bible-on-site/bible-on-site/actions/runs/37353901272/job/111912697150), the first PerekSource lookup took 70 seconds and returned an empty loading-page snapshot; the reader appeared during that request and was visible in the failure diagnostics. A 45-second polling loop could not perform a fresh lookup after the slow result. Give initial reader readiness a shared two-minute gate after session creation, capture startup failure diagnostics, and retain 45-second deadlines for all subsequent interactions. |
| VSTest mobile hang diagnostics | Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk 18.10.1; xUnit 2.9.3 | 2026-10-05 | The hang watchdog covers xUnit session initialization and diagnostic capture as well as scenario assertions. In [run 37335059230](https://github.com/bible-on-site/bible-on-site/actions/runs/37335059230/job/111848335062), iOS session creation took 268 seconds, startup assertions passed and a screenshot was saved, then the six-minute watchdog terminated the host during page-source capture while the app remained alive. The ten-minute per-test watchdog landed in #1962; retain the five-minute client startup timeout and 45-second interaction waits. Read each element's location and size once per layout check because each property access is a separate device query. [VSTest options](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/core/tools/dotnet-test-vstest). |
| Codecov TLS diagnostics | action v7; CLI 11.3.1 | 2026-10-05 | Check download and ingestion endpoints independently. The served `*.codecov.io` certificate expired at 2026-10-04 23:59:59 UTC; ingestion and API calls failed certificate validation on Windows, and CI uploads failed after retries. The official PyPI distribution can install the CLI when the binary CDN is unavailable, but cannot repair the ingestion service's certificate. At 09:32 UTC, both endpoints passed TLS validation; retrying the failed reporting job uploaded coverage successfully with signature checks, TLS validation and existing failure gates intact. [Action](https://github.com/codecov/codecov-action/blob/v7/action.yml), [wrapper](https://github.com/codecov/codecov-action/blob/v7/dist/codecov.sh). |
| XCUITest tap readiness | driver 12.15.0 | 2026-10-05 | Read `hittable` with GetAttribute: XCTest's isHittable is excluded from page XML by default. An element-relative XCTest tap returned success while the menu stayed closed on a fresh runner. The pilot now sends one W3C touch down/up pair at the observed viewport center with a 100 ms pause, below the long-press threshold. Export native Pressed/Released/Clicked and animation logs to distinguish delivery from application state. Keep native actions in the platform adapter and require the same business assertions after the touch. [Attributes](https://appium.github.io/appium-xcuitest-driver/latest/reference/element-attributes/), [gestures](https://appium.github.io/appium-xcuitest-driver/latest/guides/gestures/). |
| macOS sample | built-in macOS 26 command | 2026-10-05 | `sample <pid> 2 1 -mayDie -file <path>` records all native thread stacks for two seconds at 1 ms intervals. `-mayDie` preserves symbols when an automated app exits or crashes during collection; no UI is opened. Collect only after failed tests: background symbolication timed out and competed with healthy iOS sessions on CI. Allow two minutes for sampling and 30 seconds for process lookup. Startup checkpoints and fresh `.ips` reports locate the failing native transition when XCTest cannot retrieve the view tree. [Apple command manual](https://keith.github.io/xcode-man-pages/sample.1.html). |
| MAUI Shell content replacement | Controls 10.0.110 | 2026-10-05 | Keep startup and reading in one ShellContent to reuse its native navigation container. Clear ContentTemplate before assigning Content, otherwise ShellContent retains the templated page cache. The iOS renderer observes Content changes and replaces the page handler. Verify native startup, flyout and back navigation in both matrix jobs. [ShellContent source](https://github.com/dotnet/maui/blob/10.0.110/src/Controls/src/Core/Shell/ShellContent.cs), [iOS renderer](https://github.com/dotnet/maui/blob/10.0.110/src/Controls/src/Core/Compatibility/Handlers/Shell/iOS/ShellSectionRootRenderer.cs). |

XAML property assignment can invoke CheckedChanged before InitializeComponent finishes assigning named fields. Attach handlers that touch other named controls after initialization. | .NET Android R8 obfuscation | Microsoft.Android.Sdk 36.1.118 (workload set 10.0.402.1) | 2026-10-27 | `AndroidR8ObfuscationMode` (`disabled`|`private-members`) shipped in the .NET 10 servicing stream only from 36.1.118 — 36.1.69 and earlier silently inject `-dontobfuscate` and never emit `r8.json`, so the property is a no-op there; guard on `$(AndroidNETSdkVersion)` or fail. `private-members` switches R8 to `proguard-android-optimize.txt`, obfuscates private/package-private members, and keeps all class/interface names and public/protected members (the JNI/ACW surface in proguard_xamarin.cfg). The AAB carries `BUNDLE-METADATA/com.android.tools/r8.json` (`options.isObfuscationEnabled/isShrinkingEnabled/isOptimizationsEnabled`) and `com.android.tools.build.obfuscation/proguard.map`; Play reads both from the uploaded bundle — no separate upload step exists. Play's 25% thresholds apply to apps over 10 MB uncompressed DEX from February 2027. Verify with `app/devops/verify_android_dex_metadata.py`. |
| GitHub Actions cancellation | workflow status conditions | 2026-10-05 | Aggregate jobs need `always() && !cancelled()` to evaluate test failures while releasing the PR concurrency slot when a newer head replaces the run. An unguarded always() job may keep a cancelled workflow alive. Keep failure diagnostic upload steps on always(). If ordinary cancellation cannot finish a superseded run, the workflow-runs force-cancel API bypasses always() conditions. [GitHub API](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/actions/workflow-runs#force-cancel-a-workflow-run). |
| WebDriverAgent | 16.13.6 (locked XCUITest dependency) | 2026-10-05 | Use `appium driver run xcuitest download-wda -- --kind=sim --platform=iOS` to fetch the official agent matching the installed driver's dependency and host architecture. `usePreinstalledWDA` plus `prebuiltWDAPath` launches it without compiling inside a session. On iOS, `fullReset=true` uninstalls the application before a session. The pilot uses `noReset=false`, `fullReset=false`, and `enforceAppInstall=true` to reset and reinstall the app on the booted simulator. [Guide](https://appium.github.io/appium-xcuitest-driver/latest/guides/run-prebuilt-wda/), [capabilities](https://appium.github.io/appium-xcuitest-driver/latest/reference/capabilities/). |
| NuGet dependency snapshots | component-detection action 0.2.0; dependency-review action 5 | 2026-10-06 | The SDK labels PR snapshots with the head SHA, while default checkout scans the synthetic merge. Match source and metadata; submit the actual merge base and head with a stable correlator; the API compares their common ancestor, not necessarily the current base tip. Version-only bases can also lack graphs. Preserve the exact required `submit-nuget` check in PR and queue contexts with failing aggregate gates; reusable/matrix check names are scoped. Use one nonempty `nuget` submission. Duplicating it under the historical job name changed 2/1 snapshot counts to 3/2 without repairing the comparison; remove that ineffective trial. The review action can pass after its retry timeout with snapshot warnings still present. Verify the comparison API again after review and fail on warnings, network/HTTP errors or invalid responses; retain vulnerability and license gates. The guard remains a draft pending [GitHub historical snapshot repair](https://github.com/bible-on-site/bible-on-site/issues/2002). The supported API does not list/filter/delete historical identities. Queue/master ref duplication is unproven; do not pad counters or forge metadata. Use the named `test:dependency-snapshots`/`verify:dependency-snapshots` devops tasks; inspect reusable submission job logs directly. [Submission inputs](https://github.com/advanced-security/component-detection-dependency-submission-action/blob/v0.2.0/action.yml), [review inputs](https://github.com/actions/dependency-review-action/blob/v5/action.yml), [comparison API](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/dependency-graph/dependency-review). |
| AWS Rust SDK HTTPS features | aws-sdk-s3 1.152.0 | 2026-10-06 | The SDK's defaults enable both the current default HTTPS client and an obsolete `rustls` connector. Select `sigv4a`, `http-1x`, `default-https-client`, and `rt-tokio` explicitly to keep current behavior while removing the old TLS dependency tree. Five unit tests, a local HTTP integration test and strict Clippy pass. [SDK configuration](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sdk-for-rust/latest/dg/http.html). |
| Appium bundled dependencies | UiAutomator2 8.7.0; XCUITest 12.16.0 | 2026-10-11 | Rechecked the latest published bundles using npm 11.6.2 and 12.2.0: Android retains six vulnerable dependency families, and iOS retains shell-quote 1.10.0. Exact overrides, lockfile refresh and clean installation cannot replace `inBundle` copies. npm 12 patches explicitly exclude package manifests, so they cannot unbundle the drivers. A supported rebuilt distribution is required; track [#1995](https://github.com/bible-on-site/bible-on-site/issues/1995) and keep alerts and Renovate enabled. |

| Bun install scripts | 1.4.4 | 2026-10-26 | Dependency lifecycle scripts run only for names in `package.json` `trustedDependencies` (bun's equivalent of pnpm `allowBuilds`, not a bunfig key); blocked scripts print a warning rather than hard-fail. `bunfig.toml [install]`: `linker = "hoisted"` reproduces npm's flat node_modules (`isolated` is the pnpm-like default for workspaces), `exact = true` pins saved ranges, `minimumReleaseAge` is seconds (86400 = pnpm's 1440min default) with `minimumReleaseAgeExcludes`. Overrides use npm syntax in `package.json` — nested `{"parent": {"child": "ver"}}` works under both bun and npm; pnpm's flat `"parent>child"` key breaks `npx`/`npm`. npm's `--prefix`/`-C` maps to per-subcommand `--cwd` (`bun install --cwd <dir>`, `bun run --cwd <dir>` — no global flag); `npm ci` to `bun install --frozen-lockfile`; `npx` to `bun x`. Windows `.bin` shims are `<name>.exe`+`<name>.bunx` (no `tsc.cmd`), so `npx` misses local bins — use `bun x`. Corepack does not manage bun: install locally via `npm i -g bun`, CI via `oven-sh/setup-bun@v2`, and Docker via `COPY --from=oven/bun:<ver>-alpine@sha256:...` (pin the digest for hadolint). bun.lock is text (JSONC); bun writes no `.modules.yaml`/`.package-lock.json` marker — use `node_modules/.bin` presence to detect a completed install. `actions/setup-node` `cache:` accepts only `npm|yarn|pnpm` — `cache: bun` fails at runtime (#2643); cache Bun's store via explicit `actions/cache` on `~/.bun/install/cache` and gate the enum with `devops/github/ci/setup-node-cache.mjs`. |
| Appium | 3.8.0; .NET client 9.0.0; UiAutomator2 8.7.0; XCUITest 12.15.0 | 2026-10-04 | Install the server and drivers together through `app/mobile-e2e/bun.lock`; Appium discovers npm-managed drivers in that package. Use the default root server URL, explicit device UDIDs and fresh app sessions. Serialize scenarios within one device and parallelize platform runners through the CI matrix. Native locators and layout expectations live in platform adapters. [Client](https://github.com/appium/dotnet-client), [UiAutomator2](https://github.com/appium/appium-uiautomator2-driver). |
| Android emulator runner | 2.38.0 | 2026-10-05 | Linux CI uses KVM and an x86_64 API 36 image. Match the app RID to `android-x64` and embed assemblies in Debug APKs; Fast Deployment APKs cannot run on a fresh CI emulator. Select `-no-metrics` explicitly for unattended CI: emulator 37.2.12 warns that an unset telemetry choice will become an interactive prompt. This configures telemetry rather than disabling a test or hiding diagnostics. [Action](https://github.com/ReactiveCircus/android-emulator-runner). |
| Android AVD cache locks | emulator-runner 2.38.0 | 2026-10-28 | [Master run 40680777898](https://github.com/bible-on-site/bible-on-site/actions/runs/40680777898/job/122791950490) exited during snapshot-lock acquisition before any app test, then exhausted the unchanged boot deadline polling the absent device. [Upstream file locks](https://android.googlesource.com/platform/external/qemu/+/emu-master-dev/android/emu/files/src/android/utils/filelock.cpp) append `.lock` and store a host PID: a restored `snapshot.lock.lock` can collide with an unrelated live PID on the next runner. The failed artifact did not record its lock files, so that exact PID collision remains an inference. Treat root AVD `*.lock` entries as host state: inspect processes and ADB devices successfully, prove the selected AVD is offline, then log and remove only those locks before reuse and cache publication. Preserve payload, other AVDs and all boot/shutdown deadlines; fail closed on active or unknown ownership. Keep the existing cache key so CI exercises and diagnoses the suspect entry rather than hiding it behind a cache miss. |
| iOS boot identity handoff | Xcode 27; simctl | 2026-10-28 | [Master iOS shard 1](https://github.com/bible-on-site/bible-on-site/actions/runs/40680777898/job/122796530758) started its selected iPhone, then `ios:boot:wait` redundantly ran `simctl list devices available --json` and exhausted the existing 300-second command deadline with no output. The job had no restored simulator-cache hit, so do not attribute this to cached device corruption; the operating-system stall's cause is unproven. Pass start's successful `udid`/`version` outputs directly to wait, validate both against the SDK, and monitor that exact device with bootstatus and the native bridge. Standalone selection stays available; partial/invalid handoffs fail. Keep all deadlines and retain start/wait output in diagnostic artifacts. |
| Blocked API release selection | Node 26; GitHub published releases | 2026-10-28 | [Master CI 40680777898](https://github.com/bible-on-site/bible-on-site/actions/runs/40680777898) built and tested API 0.1.94 but skipped release after mobile startup failures. A CI-only followup's event diff does not select that API again; manual CI dispatch also cannot publish, while rerunning the old run retains its broken helpers. Reconcile only on otherwise API-unchanged master pushes against the latest published canonical API tag's immutable source. Ignore only the API's own Cargo versions, never dependency or source changes; version-only bumps remain no-ops. Select fresh API tests/build/release through unchanged quality/provenance gates, change no other module flags, and fail closed on metadata/fetch/version ambiguity. Reuse available baseline commits and preserve existing repository history depth: a depth-1 fetch in a full shared checkout changes history visibility across worktrees. New release-selection behavior requires the repository's specific AWS PR approval. |

| Bencher | CLI 0.6.13 | 2026-10-27 | A Threshold is keyed by Branch+Testbed+Measure; `bencher run` sets per-measure models via repeated `--threshold-measure/--threshold-test/--threshold-*-boundary` groups. With multiple measures, occurrences of each `--threshold-*` option zip **positionally** onto the ordered measures — every group must use the same option set and `_` explicitly unsets a value for one group; omitting an option makes that group absorb the occurrence meant for the next group (server rejected `cls_ratio` static model with a carried-over `max_sample_size: 64`). `percentage` derives each boundary limit from the historical mean, so a zero baseline collapses the upper limit to 0 and any nonzero metric alerts — the false `webvitals: CLS` alerts of #2718. CLS moved to a dedicated `cls_ratio` measure gated by a `static` upper boundary of 0.1 (the Lighthouse "good" bound), which needs no history; `--threshold-max-sample-size _` keeps the zip aligned while leaving it unset. `static` also rejects min-sample-size and window values. Alerts surface as a failing "Bencher Report" check run via `--github-actions`, not a step failure. [Threshold docs](https://bencher.dev/docs/explanation/thresholds/). |
| Playwright | 1.63.0 | 2026-10-02 | Wait for the actual lazy-loaded FlipBook after book-route reloads, not only its wrapper. Trace snapshots can slow velocity-sensitive mouse swipes; native CDP input preserves the move/release sequence without changing the tested gesture or disabling tracing. After a 30ms press, await the first native move, then queue the remaining moves and release together. This preserves Hammer's velocity sampling interval and prevents Chromium from coalescing every move into a single panstart with no panmove; that coalescing was reproduced in failed backward swipes. Avoid awaiting every move because host acknowledgements can slow the gesture. [CDPSession](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-cdpsession), [Input protocol](https://chromedevtools.github.io/devtools-protocol/tot/Input/). |

| GitHub release delivery | Actions `queue: max`; REST artifacts/jobs/deployments | 2026-10-06 | Queue release, bump and CD writers without cancelling pending work. Pin Actions artifact IDs and verify their archive digest; artifact names can be replaced by CI reruns. Use job history with `filter=all` and the published CI attempt to retain original quality evidence. Track successful target/platform delivery in Deployments. Release-by-tag lookup omits drafts: locate interrupted drafts through the authenticated paginated listing, then read and publish the release action's numeric ID only after asset verification. See [release recovery](../docs/github/workflows/ci/ci.md#draft-release-lookup-and-recovery).
